newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Government wants to give millions of "previously disadvantaged" South Africans a stake in the country's economy with a share-ownership scheme linked to the sale of state assets.

- NBS Boland sold its 25 percent stake in Norwich Holdings for 625 million rand on Thursday, in what analysts said was a precursor to a series of deals that would see the Norwich financial services group hived off and NBS Boland taking a stake in the Board of Executors Ltd.

- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel claimed success on Thursday in government's first major credibility test on economic policy because it managed to keep a tight lid on the overrun in spending this fiscal year.

- Engineering group Haggie Ltd's headline earnings plummeted 39 percent to 42 million rand for the year to end-December after the global decline in the steel industry knocked domestic and export markets.

- The hotly contested employment standards legislation looks set to become the focus of a power play between labour and government, with union federation Cosatu announcing plans on Thursday for a national stayaway on May 12 if insufficient progress is made in negotiations.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) took its lead from Wall Street on Thursday and set another trading record, spurred on by renewed confidence in the local economy and a rally in the bullion price.

- On this day a year ago, the rand started its long decline against the dollar that eventually shaved 22 percent off its value. The process reversed at the start of this year, and since then the currency has gained six percent against the dollar.
- NBS has sold its 25 percent stake in Norwich in the biggest trade on the JSE on Thursday in a bookover deal worth 625 million rand to a number of institutions.
- The South African Broadcasting Corp board is planning to relaunch Astrasat, its fledgling pay television subsidiary, Colin Hickling, the chief executive of Astrasat, said on Thursday.
SAKE BEELD
- Government will in the current fiscal year seek 2.4 billion rand more from taxpayers after it exceeded its original budget due to unforeseen circumstances.
- The sharp decline in the value of the rand is now only being felt in South Africa's inflation rate index.

- Cosatu will next week kick off a programme of mass action in response to Mininum Employment Standards legislation, possibly culminating in a general strike on May 12 if the union does not get its way.
THE STAR

- President Nelson Mandela has embarked upon a lightning round of visits to neighbouring heads of state in an urgent effort to try to resolve deepening crises in Lesotho and Swaziland and mounting instability elsewhere in the region.
- Security in South Africa's high-risk prisons is to be upgraded in an effort to halt the escape of an average of more that three prisoners a day.
